SMTO-SKL-0047 — The Drive file changed before SMTO could update it

GUID: 5a0810a0-6a7c-5a88-88bc-60ca347aa8dd
Slug: google-drive-precondition-failed
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: google-drive

What happened

  • Someone or something changed this file after SMTO last looked at it, so SMTO didn't apply its change. This avoids overwriting the newer edits.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open the file in Google Drive and see what changed, for example its name, its folder or its contents. The newer change may already do what you wanted, or may need to be kept.
  2. Ask SMTO to look up the file's latest details again before changing anything. SMTO needs the current version of the file to make a safe change.
  3. If the change is still needed, ask SMTO to make it again and approve the request. Starting from the current version means nobody's edits are overwritten.

What success looks like

  • The file in Google Drive shows your change along with the other person's edits.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. If others are editing the file right now, wait until they finish before asking again.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Drive write was refused because the file's current version or ETag differs from the supplied precondition, or Google returned HTTP 409/412.

What this means

  • Drive returns HTTP 409 or 412, or the observed version/ETag differs from the supplied write precondition. This diagnostic performs no provider access. The exact failing stage and retained receipt determine whether a request was sent; account, file or event identity must not be substituted during recovery.

Why this can happen

  • Drive returns HTTP 409 or 412, or the observed version/ETag differs from the supplied write precondition.

How to diagnose it

  • Read the exact file and compare expected version, ETag and provider conflict reason.

How to fix it

  • DriveService._write compares the pre-read file's etag/version with the supplied etag/expected_version and raises precondition_failed on mismatch; Google 409/412 (If-Match) maps to the same code. Re-read the exact file with google_drive.info, review what changed, and repeat the edit with its current version or ETag only if it is still wanted.
  • Read the exact file again with google_drive.info, review its state and use its current version or available ETag.

Retry and execution caution

  • Read the exact file again with google_drive.info, review its state and use its current version or available ETag.

How to verify the fix

  • A deliberate edit uses current observed preconditions after resolving the conflict.

What not to do

  • Do not expose credentials, content or resumable URLs.
  • Do not blindly repeat uncertain writes.

Technical notes

  • This diagnostic performs no provider access. The exact failing stage and retained receipt determine whether a request was sent; account, file or event identity must not be substituted during recovery.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
